commands.summary: decisions/0045-deterministic-semantic-extraction-substrate-and-rog-schema-v2.md binds Tree-sitter selection (evaluated against language-specific stacks on determinism/incremental capability/malformed-input behavior/cancellation/portability/packaging/license/maintenance), the schema-v2 vocabulary (Symbol+SymbolKind, Defines/Imports/Exports/Implements/Extends/References/Calls/UsesType edge kinds, GraphSourceLocation), stable symbol identity, and the parser-neutral SemanticAdapter boundary.

commands.command: Focused compatibility test proving the schema hazard, before implementation
commands.summary: repopact_graph::durable::tests confirmed a v1-shaped reader hard-fails deserializing a shard line naming an unrecognized node/edge kind string -- the concrete evidence justifying the schema-major bump to 2 rather than silent variant addition under version 1.

commands.command: MSRV/version research against the live crates.io index
commands.summary: tree-sitter 0.27.0 declares rust-version 1.90 (cargo info); RepoPact has no documented MSRV contract anywhere in the repository; installed toolchain is rustc/cargo 1.96.0. Grammar crate versions confirmed live: tree-sitter-rust 0.24.2, tree-sitter-python 0.25.0, tree-sitter-javascript 0.25.0, tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2. All pinned exactly (=X.Y.Z) in rust/Cargo.toml.

commands.command: Real Tree-sitter spike (scratch crate, not committed)
commands.summary: Compiled all five crates together and parsed real Rust/Python/JavaScript/TypeScript/TSX source into the expected distinct root node kinds. Separately proved parse_with_options + a progress callback returning ControlFlow::Break cancels a parse of 200,000 repeated lines (returns None), and Parser::reset() + reuse succeeds afterward for an unrelated parse -- confirmed there is no deprecated set_timeout_micros symbol anywhere in tree-sitter 0.27.0's source.

commands.command: Grounding spikes for each grammar's real AST shape (scratch crates, not committed)
commands.summary: Dumped real tree-sitter-rust/-python/-javascript/-typescript output for representative source before writing any adapter code. Caught and fixed a real bug this way during test-writing: the Rust #[test] attribute's inner AST node kind is "attribute" (bare identifier text), not "identifier"/"scoped_identifier" as first assumed -- so plain #[test] was initially unrecognized while only #[tokio::test]-shaped attributes matched. Fixed and covered by a dedicated test before this evidence was recorded.

43/43 tests pass, including: Rust/Python/JS/TS/TSX symbol coverage per language; TS-vs-TSX proven as genuinely distinct grammars (JSX syntax parses under TSX, fails under plain TypeScript); stable IDs unaffected by leading blank lines/comments; every semantic edge carries layer/derivation/location; import edges point to fact nodes carrying raw import text, never a fabricated resolved target; malformed input yields Partial coverage not a crash; a near-zero parse deadline genuinely cancels a large parse and the parser is reusable afterward; a recursion-depth guard (added mid-session after re-checking ROG-022's full text) truncates 2000-level pathological nesting instead of overflowing the walker's own call stack; unsupported-language/oversized/binary files are distinct, correctly classified coverage states; one malformed file does not remove valid output from unrelated files in the same build, and a corrected rebuild clears the gap deterministically; repository-wide Freshness::Partial is genuinely emitted for a real coverage gap and NOT emitted for expected unsupported-language/policy exclusions alone; a genuine schema-v1 manifest remains readable and a v1-graph full rebuild deterministically produces valid schema-v2 output; the WI057 bounded-git-invocation test remains <=4 after semantic extraction.
Full workspace green, including the Tauri desktop build (tree-sitter's native C grammar sources compile cleanly into every target); repopact-validation's 49 tests unaffected.

commands.command: Real RepoPact self-build (engineering validation, not S8/R1)
commands.summary: repopact graph build --root . against RepoPact's own live checkout: 18.2s wall-clock, 749 files considered, 106 files actually adapted (Rust/Python/JS/TS), 106/106 complete (0 partial, 0 failed, 0 policy-skipped), 643 correctly classified as unsupported-language (docs/config/data files). Result: schema_version=2, node_count=4481 (governance=773, physical=954, semantic=2754), edge_count=6122 (governance=1583, physical=1738, semantic=2801), 16/16 node and edge shards, durable graph 4.0MB on disk. repopact graph verify reported Fresh. Canonical `repopact validate` accepted the live durable graph with zero diagnostics. The rog/ directory produced by this run was deleted afterward -- not committed, per this checkpoint's scope (engineering validation, not a deliverable artifact).

A 7-file fixture (Rust with a module/test/function, Python with a class/function/test, JavaScript, TypeScript with an interface, TSX with JSX, one malformed-but-recoverable Rust file, one unsupported README.md), confirmed byte-identical by SHA-256 of every source file, was independently built via the raw engine stdio protocol on native Windows (C:\Projects\repopact checkout) and a Linux-native WSL2 Debian 13 checkout (~/repopact-linux, never /mnt/c/...). Result: byte-for-byte identical source_projection_fingerprint (12e09a011f0a89073cb22e25acc52ccb57867445ec35d3e5242064d35eb899a2), node_count (18), edge_count (17), every one of 10 node and 11 edge shard SHA-256 hashes, and identical semantic_coverage (7 files considered, 5 complete, 1 partial [the malformed Rust file], 1 unsupported-language). No macOS execution occurred or is claimed.

repopact_graph's randomized_git_invocation_count_is_still_bounded_after_graph_build test (<=4 invocations) passes unchanged after semantic extraction was added; the orchestrator processes files sequentially in a single thread, spawning no per-file threads or processes; each adapter parse constructs one Parser instance per call, never one native parser per source file left resident.

repopact-engine.exe release build: 6,955,520 bytes before this checkpoint (Decision 0044-only, WI046 baseline) vs 12,073,984 bytes after (Tree-sitter core + 4 grammar crates linked in) -- a +5,118,464 byte (+73.6%) increase. No system Tree-sitter install, libclang, or runtime grammar download is required anywhere; all parsing capability is compiled directly into the released binary.
Canonical Rust validation, the explicit Python legacy comparator, and conformance (6 passed, 18 subtests) all pass on the live checkout (graph-disabled, as no rog/ is committed).

closeout.decision_0045: accepted -- Tree-sitter selected with exact pinned versions; schema v2 bound additively over v1
closeout.msrv_conclusion: tree-sitter 0.27.0 requires rustc 1.90; RepoPact has no prior documented MSRV; this session establishes 1.90 as the workspace's de facto floor
closeout.schema_v1_compatibility: proven: a genuine v1 manifest (physical-only vocabulary) remains structurally valid and Fresh under the schema-v2-aware validator; a v1 graph's only supported migration (full deterministic rebuild) produces valid v2 output

Left pending on those specific, disclosed gaps.

The architecture review's rollout plan favors (b) once full-build output is itself stable, which this checkpoint has now proven cross-platform; a fresh Sol-level review should decide between closing the disclosed gaps first versus proceeding to incremental update.
